title: Bakar Ikan
mood: a family with only one question
subject: grilling skipjack on an Ambon beach with every cousin who came home
caption: Eastern Indonesian party pop in the Lagu Timur style. A rubbery, bouncy synth bass carrying a syncopated tropical groove, light Latin-leaning percussion with shakers and congas, a clean electric guitar picking short melodic hooks, hand claps on the chorus, no kendang and no suling. Warm, swinging and light, built for dancing rather than loudness. Relaxed male voice singing in Ambon Malay dialect with light autotune, answered by a group in call-and-response on the chorus. 98 BPM, A major. A family that asks only one question. No dangdut koplo rhythm, no kendang, no trap drums, no ballad section, no key change.
lyrics:
[Intro - synth bass and tropical percussion]

[Verse 1]
Sore di pantai Ambon, sepupu semua datang
Ikan cakalang di atas bara, sambal colo-colo dalam toples
Om Yopi pegang kipas, dia bilang "jang ganggu"
Dari kecil dia yang bakar, sampai sekarang dia yang bakar

[Chorus - call and response]
Bakar ikan, bakar ikan, dong samua datang
Seng ada yang tanya kerja apa, seng ada yang tanya kapan kawin
Cuma satu yang ditanya: "su makan?"
Kalau balom, dudu, ambil piring

[Verse 2]
Sepupu dari Jakarta su lupa logat
Dua jam di sini, logatnya pulang sendiri
Kami tertawa, dia tertawa paling keras
Dia bilang dia rindu, dia bilang itu waktu matahari su turun

[Chorus - call and response]
Bakar ikan, bakar ikan, dong samua datang
Seng ada yang tanya kerja apa, seng ada yang tanya kapan kawin
Cuma satu yang ditanya: "su makan?"
Kalau balom, dudu, ambil piring, ambil dua

[Outro - percussion fades]
Matahari turun
Om Yopi masih bakar
